title: What enforcement found
question: What have the Ethics Commission, prosecutors and the City Attorney put in writing about lobbying, gifts and contributions?
finding: The Ethics Commission’s penalty list holds 12 lobbying cases ($58,168 in penalties), 10 gift cases and 14 cases about contribution limits or contributions from City contractors. The largest lobbying penalty is $16,000 (Gwyneth Borden, 2023). The document library also holds 33 announcements by federal and local prosecutors and the City Attorney of charges, pleas or sentences for bribes and gratuities to City officials.
how: Every case on the Ethics Commission’s list of penalties whose category is lobbying, or whose violation text cites the lobbying, gift, contractor-contribution or contribution-limit rules, with the Commission’s own description quoted in at most twelve words. Court items are the prosecutors’ and City Attorney’s announcements in this project’s document library whose titles mention bribery, gratuities, corruption or honest-services fraud; the first twelve words of each title are quoted.
limits: These are findings by an authority, most of them settlements in which the respondent agreed to the facts. A penalty for a late or incomplete report is not a finding that the lobbying itself was improper. An announcement of charges is an accusation; the later plea, verdict or dismissal is a separate row where the library holds it. The list is only what was caught and resolved; conduct nobody reported or audited does not appear.
